bio-gen-01-c1.text: National Human Genome Research Institute. Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA). Talking Glossary of Genomic and Genetic Terms, genome.gov.
bio-gen-01-c1.quote: adenine bonds with thymine, and cytosine bonds with guanine.
bio-gen-01-c1.claim: A always pairs with T, and G always pairs with C.

bio-gen-01-c1.text: King's College London. The story behind Photograph 51. King's College London.
bio-gen-01-c1.quote: Photograph 51, and other data from Rosalind’s work during her time at King’s, were key to building the structure of DNA
bio-gen-01-c1.claim: Watson and Crick worked this out in 1953 using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data.

bio-gen-01-c2.text: National Human Genome Research Institute. Exome. Talking Glossary of Genomic and Genetic Terms, genome.gov.
bio-gen-01-c2.quote: In humans, the exome is about 1.5% of the genome.
bio-gen-01-c2.claim: Only about 1.5% of human DNA codes for proteins.

bio-gen-02-c3.text: Baba P. D. Inusa, Lewis L. Hsu, Neeraj Kohli, et al (2019). Sickle Cell Disease: Genetics, Pathophysiology, Clinical Presentation and Treatment. International Journal of Neonatal Screening.
bio-gen-02-c3.quote: A single base-pair point mutation (GAG to GTG) results in the substitution of the amino acid glutamic acid (hydrophilic) to Valine (hydrophobic) in the 6th position of the β-chain of haemoglobin referred to as haemoglobin S (HbS)
bio-gen-02-c3.claim: Sickle-cell anaemia is caused by a single missense mutation in haemoglobin: GAG → GTG, changing glutamate to valine and distorting the protein's shape.

bio-gen-04-c2.text: Bastiaan T. Heijmans, Elmar W. Tobi, Aryeh D. Stein, et al (2008). Persistent epigenetic differences associated with prenatal exposure to famine in humans. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
bio-gen-04-c2.quote: Here we show that individuals who were prenatally exposed to famine during the Dutch Hunger Winter in 1944–45 had, 6 decades later, less DNA methylation of the imprinted IGF2 gene compared with their unexposed, same-sex siblings.
bio-gen-04-c2.claim: The Dutch Hunger Winter (1944–45) showed that famine experienced in the womb left epigenetic marks affecting metabolism decades later.

bio-gen-04-c3.text: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2006. NobelPrize.org.
bio-gen-04-c3.quote: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2006 was awarded jointly to Andrew Z. Fire and Craig C. Mello "for their discovery of RNA interference - gene silencing by double-stranded RNA"
bio-gen-04-c3.claim: RNAi was discovered by Andrew Fire and Craig Mello, who won the 2006 Nobel Prize.

bio-gen-05-c1.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (2020). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020. NobelPrize.org.
bio-gen-05-c1.quote: Her work showed that tracrRNA is part of bacteria’s ancient immune system, CRISPR/Cas, that disarms viruses by cleaving their DNA.
bio-gen-05-c1.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 is a genome-editing tool adapted from a bacterial immune system.

bio-gen-05-c1.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (2020). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020. NobelPrize.org.
bio-gen-05-c1.quote: Using the CRISPR/Cas9 genetic scissors, it is now possible to change the code of life over the course of a few weeks.
bio-gen-05-c1.claim: A single researcher can now edit a gene in weeks rather than years.

bio-gen-05-c2.text: (2023). FDA Approves First Gene Therapies to Treat Patients with Sickle Cell Disease. U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
bio-gen-05-c2.quote: Casgevy is the first FDA-approved therapy utilizing CRISPR/Cas9, a type of genome editing technology.
bio-gen-05-c2.claim: In 2023, Casgevy became the first approved CRISPR-based therapy: it cures sickle-cell disease and beta-thalassaemia by reactivating the foetal haemoglobin gene, bypassing the defective adult haemoglobin gene.

bio-gen-05-c3.text: Henry T. Greely (2019). CRISPR’d babies: human germline genome editing in the ‘He Jiankui affair’. Journal of Law and the Biosciences.
bio-gen-05-c3.quote: The world was shocked in Nov. 25, 2018 by the revelation that He Jiankui had used clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (‘CRISPR’) to edit embryos
bio-gen-05-c3.claim: In 2018, He Jiankui shocked the scientific community by creating the first gene-edited babies: twin girls with CCR5 mutations intended to confer HIV resistance.

bio-gen-06-c3.text: Yuanjun Lu, Yau-Tuen Chan, Hor-Yue Tan, et al (2020). Epigenetic regulation in human cancer: the potential role of epi-drug in cancer therapy. Molecular Cancer.
bio-gen-06-c3.quote: Currently, three general hydroxamic acid HDACIs have been approved by FDA: (i) Vorinostat (SAHA) which is responsible for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL)
bio-gen-06-c3.claim: HDAC inhibitors (vorinostat, romidepsin) treat cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

bio-gen-07-c3.text: Genetics vs. Genomics Fact Sheet. National Human Genome Research Institute.
bio-gen-07-c3.quote: All human beings are 99.9 percent identical in their genetic makeup.
bio-gen-07-c3.claim: Two random humans typically differ at ~3 million sites in their 3-billion-base genomes: about 0.1%.

bio-gen-08-c1.text: Human Genome Project Fact Sheet. National Human Genome Research Institute.
bio-gen-08-c1.quote: Carried out from 1990–2003, it was one of the most ambitious and important scientific endeavors in human history.
bio-gen-08-c1.claim: The Human Genome Project (1990-2003) produced the first reference human genome.

bio-gen-08-c2.text: Innocent G. Asiimwe, Munir Pirmohamed (2022). Ethnic Diversity and Warfarin Pharmacogenomics. Frontiers in Pharmacology.
bio-gen-08-c2.quote: As shown in Figure 1, CYP2C9 encodes an enzyme that metabolizes the more potent enantiomer of warfarin (S-warfarin) while VKORC1 encodes warfarin’s molecular target.
bio-gen-08-c2.claim: Genetic variants in drug-metabolizing enzymes (CYPs especially) and drug targets explain why people respond differently to the same dose.

bio-gen-08-c3.text: Christi J. Guerrini, Jill O. Robinson, Devan Petersen, Amy L. McGuire (2018). Should police have access to genetic genealogy databases? Capturing the Golden State Killer and other criminals using a controversial new forensic technique. PLOS Biology.
bio-gen-08-c3.quote: Using a novel forensic approach, investigators identified the suspect by first identifying his relatives using a free, online genetic database populated by individuals researching their family trees.
bio-gen-08-c3.claim: The Golden State Killer case (2018) used a genealogy database to identify a suspect from distant relatives' DNA.

bio-gen-02-c2.text: Suzanne Clancy, William Brown (2008). Translation: DNA to mRNA to Protein. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-gen-02-c2.quote: There are three termination codons that are employed at the end of a protein-coding sequence in mRNA: UAA, UAG, and UGA.
bio-gen-02-c2.claim: When a stop codon (UAA, UAG, or UGA) is reached, the chain is released.

bio-gen-03-c1.text: Ilona Miko (2008). Gregor Mendel and the Principles of Inheritance. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-gen-03-c1.quote: Our modern understanding of how traits may be inherited through generations comes from the principles proposed by Gregor Mendel in 1865.
bio-gen-03-c1.claim: Gregor Mendel, working with pea plants in the 1860s, deduced two fundamental laws of heredity.

bio-gen-03-c2.text: Ilona Miko (2008). Genetic Dominance: Genotype-Phenotype Relationships. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-gen-03-c2.quote: Complete dominance occurs when the heterozygote phenotype is indistinguishable from that of the homozygous parent.
bio-gen-03-c2.claim: In complete dominance, one allele fully masks the other.

bio-gen-03-c3.text: Maria Jackson, Leah Marks, Gerhard H. W. May, Joanna B. Wilson (2018). The genetic basis of disease. Essays in Biochemistry.
bio-gen-03-c3.quote: Females who are heterozygous, carrying one copy of a pathogenic variant allele, are generally asymptomatic and thus haemophilia shows a typical X-linked recessive inheritance pattern
bio-gen-03-c3.claim: Red-green colour blindness and haemophilia are X-linked recessive.

bio-gen-06-c1.text: Theresa Phillips (2008). The Role of Methylation in Gene Expression. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-gen-06-c1.quote: Today, researchers know that DNA methylation occurs at the cytosine bases of eukaryotic DNA, which are converted to 5-methylcytosine by DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) enzymes.
bio-gen-06-c1.claim: DNA methylation: methyl groups on cytosine nucleotides (especially in CpG dinucleotides) typically silence genes.

bio-gen-06-c2.text: Jennifer Ahn, Jeannie Lee (2008). X Chromosome: X Inactivation. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-gen-06-c2.quote: The patchy distribution of color on calico cats results from the random inactivation of one X chromosome in females.
bio-gen-06-c2.claim: This produces calico cat coat patterns (different X-linked color genes silenced in patches of cells).

bio-gen-07-c1.text: Richard Kliman, Bob Sheehy, Joanna Schultz (2008). Genetic Drift and Effective Population Size. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-gen-07-c1.quote: Moreover, scientists are well aware of the fact that real-life populations are not infinite, as the Hardy-Weinberg model requires us to assume.
bio-gen-07-c1.claim: The Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium describes the null state: in an infinitely large randomly mating population without selection or mutation, allele frequencies stay constant.

bio-gen-07-c2.text: Richard Kliman, Bob Sheehy, Joanna Schultz (2008). Genetic Drift and Effective Population Size. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-gen-07-c2.quote: Drift is more pronounced in such populations, because smaller populations have less variation and, therefore, a lower ability to respond favorably
bio-gen-07-c2.claim: Genetic drift is strongest in small populations: this explains why isolated island populations or those passing through bottlenecks (founder events) lose diversity.
